identification.summary: Red Nue is the Malpedia/MISP name for a China-linked (Chinese-speaking) espionage cluster that TeamT5 and Kaspersky track as LuoYu [S1][S2][S3]. It is associated with the multi-platform LootRAT/ReverseWindow backdoor (Windows and macOS variants reported as Demsty; Android variant SpyDealer) and the Windows backdoor WinDealer [S1][S5]. TeamT5 presented the group at JSAC in January 2021 [S5]. Kaspersky reported in June 2022 that WinDealer is delivered through man-on-the-side interception of application update requests [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: Dates differ by source: TeamT5 (via JPCERT/CC conference coverage) says activity has been observed since 2014 [S5]; Kaspersky and BlackBerry say since at least 2008 [S2][S4]; Malpedia says active since at least 2017 and WinDealer in use since at least 2019 [S1].
identification.notes: Aliases: Red Nue (Malpedia/MISP) and LuoYu (TeamT5, Kaspersky) [S1][S2]. No Microsoft Typhoon/Storm name was found in the sources gathered. The Malpedia 2017 start date conflicts with the vendor 2008/2014 dates; do not merge them [S1][S2][S5].

attribution.confidence: Kaspersky characterizes LuoYu as a Chinese-speaking APT actor [S2]; BlackBerry describes it as a sophisticated APT group linked to China [S4]. No source gathered attributes the group to a specific PRC government agency or contractor.
attribution.basis: Shared C2 servers tied samples across ReverseWindow, WinDealer and SpyDealer, per TeamT5's JSAC 2021 presentation as summarized in secondary coverage [S5]. Kaspersky later confirmed the Demsty-WinDealer link [S3]. Language and target profile are Kaspersky's basis for 'Chinese-speaking' [S2].

objectives: Espionage against organizations in and around China, including foreign diplomatic organizations in China, academia, and defense, logistics, telecommunications and financial companies [S2][S6]. WinDealer functions include file search and transfer, screenshots and command execution, consistent with information collection [S3].

regions: China (vast majority of victims per Kaspersky)
Germany, Austria, United States, Czech Republic, Russia, India (Kaspersky)
Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan (per TeamT5)
targeting.notes: Kaspersky says the vast majority of LuoYu victims are in China, with additional victims in several other countries [S2]. TeamT5's sector and region list comes from JPCERT/CC conference summaries [S5]. Malpedia notes the 2019 WinDealer watering hole on a Chinese news website serving the diaspora [S1]. Diplomatic and academic groups are described as targets, not named victims [S2].

capabilities.summary: Multi-platform toolset: ReverseWindow/LootRAT (Windows, macOS as Demsty), SpyDealer (Android) and WinDealer (Windows); TeamT5 also lists Linux and Mac targeting [S1][S5]. WinDealer is modular and can capture screenshots, run commands, transfer files, search documents and perform ping-scan discovery [S3]. Its 2020 sample has no hard-coded C2 and instead generates addresses from a pool of about 48,000 ChinaNet addresses in Xizang and Guizhou [S6]. Delivery includes watering holes (including local news sites), and from about 2020 man-on-the-side replacement of update downloads for popular Asian apps such as QQ and WeChat [S2][S3][S6]. BlackBerry also describes man-on-the-side combined with watering-hole attacks on Android messaging apps [S4]. Kaspersky speculates the actor may be intercepting traffic at network level so it needs no real C2 servers [S6].

diamond.adversary: Chinese-speaking espionage actor tracked as LuoYu (TeamT5, Kaspersky) and Red Nue (Malpedia/MISP); no named sponsor in sources [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: WinDealer, ReverseWindow/LootRAT/Demsty, SpyDealer; watering holes and man-on-the-side update hijacking [S1][S3][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: WinDealer picks C2 from about 48,000 ChinaNet addresses (Xizang, Guizhou) via an address-generation algorithm, with no fixed C2 [S6]; shared C2 servers linked the malware families [S5].
diamond.victim: Foreign diplomatic organizations in China, academia, defense, logistics, telecommunications and finance; mostly in China, plus several other countries [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Intelligence collection on foreign missions and sensitive sectors in and near China; diaspora-focused watering hole in 2019 [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Software auto-update channels of popular Asian applications and unencrypted or interceptable network paths; Android messaging apps [S4][S6].

gaps: Securelist, JPCERT/CC and BlackBerry pages could not be opened (fetch blocked); facts rely on search excerpts and secondary coverage (Kaspersky press release, The Hacker News, Security Affairs) and should be checked against the originals.
Sponsor is not identified by any gathered source.
No Microsoft name mapping found; no MITRE group ID.
Activity after 2022 was not found in the sources gathered.
The PwC reports listed in the original record were not reviewed.
Named victims and the network position enabling man-on-the-side interception are not public in gathered sources.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the software update path of popular regional applications, news sites popular with diaspora communities, and Android messaging apps used by personnel [S3][S4][S1]. STEP 2: The actor needs only an internet-connected victim for man-on-the-side delivery, so users on untrusted or in-country networks are exposed [S6]. STEP 3: Template is update-request interception or watering hole, then WinDealer or Demsty, then document search, screenshots and file transfer to dynamically generated C2 addresses [S3][S6]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued collection against diplomatic and academic targets in China and Asia. MDCOA is use of update hijacking against travelers or deployed personnel on regional networks. Candidate indicators: application update downloads from unexpected sources or failing signature checks, and outbound connections to many ChinaNet addresses in Xizang or Guizhou [S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: personnel on China-region networks and personal Android devices are exposed; track travel and device policy. (2) Authorities: network-level interception occurs outside friendly networks, so response is limited to endpoint and policy measures. (3) Mission assurance: restrict auto-update of unmanaged applications on mission systems and enforce signed-update verification. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partners and diplomatic security elements, noting the sources are largely secondary and need validation.

provenance.importedSummary: Red Nue, active since at least 2017, is known for its use of the multi-platform LootRAt backdoor, also known as ReverseWindow. LootRAT has variants for Windows and Macintosh (reported in open source as Demsty), as well as an Android variant known as SpyDealer. Red Nue has also used another Windows backdoor known as WinDealer since at least 2019, when it deployed it to targets as part of a watering hole campaign on a Chinese news website for the Chinese diaspora community. Parts of Asia feature heavily in Red Nue's victimology.
